technique_name: Describe the circumstances under which a person can be released on bail
description: In most criminal cases, a judge can grant release on bail if they determine that the accused individual is not a flight risk or a danger to the community. Generally, an individual who is deemed a low risk will be allowed to remain free until their trial while they await their court dates. In some instances, prosecutors may require the accused person to pay a deposit or sign a bail bond in order to remain free. This requires the accused person to promise that they will appear in court or forfeit
